title: NIST ARIA 0.1 Pilot Evaluation Report — Phase 65 NIST ARIA assurance adoption review
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the NIST ARIA assurance adoption reporting pack. NIST documents a pilot involving five organizations, seven AI applications, three scenarios, and model, red-team, and field-testing levels.
key_findings: The pilot exercised three distinct evaluation levels.
Measurement trees were used to assess application validity.
The sample is intentionally small and exploratory.
why_it_matters: Which records connect evaluation design and authorization to monitoring, incidents, correction, independent review, institutional use, and outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. This is the strongest current pathway record for a completed multi-level AI evaluation procedure.
ftfn_relevance: Advances one named Phase 55Y reader journey.
Separates the current evidence stage from downstream operation or outcome claims.
Creates a specific next-record watch point.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
A pilot procedure is not a generally accepted assurance standard.
The report does not validate AI systems outside the submitted applications.
